title: Your Body Makes 2 Million Blood Cells Every Second
sources: Stanford Blood Center, The Life of a Red Blood Cell: marrow makes ~2 million new red cells each second, lifespan ~120 days
LibreTexts Anatomy & Physiology 16.2C RBC Life Cycle: ~2 million/second, 100-120 day lifespan; textbook arithmetic ~25 trillion cells in 5 L of blood
American Red Cross: red cells are replaced within about 4-8 weeks after donating blood

lines.text: Right now, your body is building two million new blood cells. Every single second.
That is about one hundred seventy billion a day, made deep inside your bones.
Each red cell laps your whole body about once a minute, carrying oxygen.
Then it wears out after about one hundred twenty days.
So the red cells in you right now will all be gone in four months.
You carry about twenty-five trillion of them at any moment.
Even after you give a pint of blood, your body usually rebuilds those red cells within weeks.
So is the blood in your veins the same blood you had last year?
